summary: A lookout has stood on Mount Harris since 1930; the current 40-foot tower dates from 1957 and is standing but listed as abandoned.

facts.design: 40-foot open timber tower with a live-in cab
facts.status_note: Still standing but listed as abandoned; radio equipment is mounted on and around it.

staffing.status: No staffing found after 1954; Forest Lookouts names Al Geiss as the lookout in August 1937, and firelookout.com names Florence Beck in 1954.

visit.trail_note: A 2012 visit describes a rough road, left partway, then a hike of about 1.8 miles to the top.

Forest Lookouts dates a 14x14 cab on a 30-foot tower to 1942; firelookout.com dates the wooden tower to the late 1930s.
Rock blasted near the top to widen and improve the road to the lookout.
Florence Beck listed as lookout personnel.
A new radio repeater installed on the mountain.
Current 40-foot tower with live-in cab built at a slightly different location, replacing the earlier tower.
Old lookout tower dismantled; salvaged material used for a repeater building under the new tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says a 30-foot wooden live-in tower was built in the late 1930s; Forest Lookouts dates a 14x14 cab on a 30-foot tower to 1942. Not resolved; both are reported.
NHLR describes an open timber tower, Forest Lookouts a laminated structure, and firelookout.com a treated timber tower. Not resolved; the story says so.
The Forest Fire Lookout Association list says Tower Standing, while the 2012 visit records the lookout as abandoned. Both hold: the tower stands but is abandoned.

sources.title: Mt. Harris – Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Brief had no height; height_m 12.2 is 40 feet converted to metres. Access level omitted: no source states whether the site is public or closed; the 2012 account describes a rough road and a hike of about 1.8 miles. Second-tower date (late 1930s vs 1942) and 1957 construction material are unresolved. No staffing record after 1954 found. A 2012 account is the newest status evidence.
